newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN STOCKS END HIGHER IN TECHNICAL REBOUND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN STOCKS END HIGHER IN TECHNICAL REBOUND.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Thursday in a technical rebound after three straight days of heavy falls, brokers said.

The index opened up 1.08 percent to an intraday high of 9,659.69 points, then drifted lower to negative territory before recovering to close at 9,632.34, a gain of 76.22 points or 0.80 percent. Turnover was modest at T$144.3 billion.
Electronics led the rebound, gaining 1.89 percent as Nasdaq, especially U.S. semiconductor equipment makers, rebouned overnight. Microchip maker United Microelectronics was up T$3.5 to T$123.5.

Microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor ended unchanged at T$142.5 amid caution. It fell by the daily seven percent limit to T$142.5 on Wednesday after Dutch electronics giant Philips Electronics NV's announcement to auction 100 million shares of Taiwan Semicon on August 18.
"Helped by Nasdaq's rebound overnight, the index launched a technical rebound," said National Securities analyst Oliver Fang. "But we can see caution in the rebound as turnover did not expand much."
Institutaional investors' net buying during Wednesday's 2.57 percent plunge also helped sentiment, Fang said.
Textiles rose 1.85 percent, with textile giant Hualon up T$1.3 to T$28.2.
Electricals and constructions were also strong, but financial and car shares fell.
Brokers said they expected consolidation ahead. For Friday, a 9,550-9,700 range was seen. -- Taipei newsroom (886) 2-508-0815; Fax (886) 2-508-0204 -- Email: taipei.newsroom@reuters.com
